title: Singapore's Indian-Origin Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon to Retire in February 2027
excerpt: Menon, Singapore's first locally born Chief Justice, will step down after more than 14 years on the bench. Justice Sushil Nair has been appointed as the country's fifth Chief Justice.
body:
• Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon will retire on February 26, 2027, a day after his 65th birthday, ending over 14 years in the role
  • Justice Sushil Sukumaran Nair, also of Indian origin, has been appointed as Singapore's fifth Chief Justice
  • Menon was Singapore's first locally born Chief Justice and the second to have served as Attorney-General
  • The announcement was made by Singapore's Prime Minister's Office on July 17, 2026

Singapore's Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon will retire on February 26, 2027, the Prime Minister's Office announced on July 17. Menon, who is of Indian origin, has served as the city-state's fourth Chief Justice since November 2012 — the longest-serving occupant of the role in modern Singapore.

Justice Sushil Sukumaran Nair, a Justice of the Court of Appeal, has been appointed as Singapore's fifth Chief Justice with effect from February 26, 2027. The appointment was made by President Tharman Shanmugaratnam, acting in concurrence with the advice of Prime Minister Lawrence Wong.

A Transformative Tenure

Menon, born on February 26, 1962, will step down a day after his 65th birthday — the constitutional retirement age for Singapore's judiciary. During his more than 14 years as Chief Justice, Menon led what the PMO described as "a period of significant transformation" for Singapore's judiciary.

He oversaw the establishment of the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) in 2015, which strengthened Singapore's position as a hub for international dispute resolution. He led the judiciary's digital transformation, established the Appellate Division of the High Court, and introduced a therapeutic justice approach in the Family Justice Courts and Youth Courts.

"Chief Justice Menon has served Singapore with distinction over the past 14 years. Under his leadership, our Judiciary has earned the confidence of Singaporeans and the respect of the international legal community."

— Prime Minister Lawrence Wong

Menon also established the Singapore Judicial College as the cornerstone of judicial education. Educated at the National University of Singapore and Harvard Law School, he was a founding partner of WongPartnership and served as Attorney-General before joining the bench.

His Successor: Justice Sushil Nair

Justice Sushil Sukumaran Nair, also of Indian descent, brings a distinguished background in corporate restructuring. He spent 35 years at Drew & Napier LLC, serving as Deputy Chief Executive Officer and Head of the firm's Corporate Restructuring and Workouts practice group. Chambers Asia Pacific ranked him in Band 1 for Restructuring and Insolvency for 17 consecutive years.

Nair joined the bench as Judicial Commissioner in April 2025, was appointed High Court Judge in March 2026, and elevated to Justice of the Court of Appeal in June 2026 — a rapid ascent through Singapore's judicial hierarchy.

Beyond legal practice, Nair was awarded Singapore's Public Service Star (COVID-19) in 2023 for conceptualising the framework of the country's COVID-19 Temporary Measures Bill, which was passed by Parliament in April 2020 and provided critical relief to businesses and individuals during the pandemic. He also received the Friends of MCCY Award in 2022 for his role in the Singapore Sports Hub takeover.

Two Indian-Origin Chief Justices in Succession

The succession from Menon to Nair means Singapore will have two consecutive Chief Justices of Indian origin — a detail of particular significance for the Indian diaspora in Southeast Asia. Menon was Singapore's first locally born Chief Justice and the first of Indian descent to hold the position. His predecessor, Chan Sek Keong, was of Chinese descent.

Singapore's Indian community, which constitutes roughly 9 percent of the resident population, has historically been well-represented in the legal profession. The appointments reflect both the community's depth of legal talent and Singapore's meritocratic approach to judicial selection.

Legacy and Context

Under Menon's leadership, Singapore's judiciary has consistently ranked among the world's most efficient and trusted. The World Bank's Ease of Doing Business rankings, the World Economic Forum's competitiveness reports, and international arbitration surveys have repeatedly cited Singapore's courts as a model for commercial dispute resolution.

Menon's advocacy for the internationalisation of Singapore law and his writings on transnational justice and legal pluralism have also contributed to academic discourse on the judiciary's role in a globalised world.

What's Next

Justice Nair will assume the role of Chief Justice on February 26, 2027. His background in complex commercial and cross-border restructuring cases is expected to further strengthen Singapore's appeal as a centre for international legal services. The Prime Minister's Office expressed confidence that Nair will "build on these strong foundations and continue to uphold the excellence, integrity and independence" of Singapore's judiciary.
